data.title: Anutin miffed at 2.2% GDP growth forecast
data.description: <p>Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul and Finance Minister Ekniti Nitithanprapas have said Thailand's projected 2.2% economic growth this year is still far from satisfactory, arguing that the country should aim for growth of 3-6%.</p>

data.title: Akanat defends energy permanent secretary pick
data.description: <p>Energy Minister Akanat Promphan has defended Chantanon Wannakejohn's appointment as permanent secretary, rejecting claims it was politically motivated.</p>

data.title: OCPB ramps up plane seat inquiry
data.description: <p>Prime Minister's Office Minister Supamas Isarabhakdi has ordered the Office of the Consumer Protection Board (OCPB) to broaden its probe into airline overbooking after a passenger was denied boarding despite checking in on time.</p>

data.title: PP urges EC to send senate election case to top court
data.description: <p>The main opposition People's Party (PP) has urged the Election Commission (EC) to refer a case involving alleged collusion in the 2024 Senate election to the Supreme Court, warning that the poll agency's credibility is already "almost gone".</p>

data.title: EEC expansion plan 'must be transparent'
data.description: <p>Opposition leader Natthaphong Ruengpanyawut has called on Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul to ensure transparency over the proposed expansion of the Eastern Economic Corridor (EEC) into Prachin Buri province.</p>

data.title: Anutin pitches Asean gateway
data.description: <p>Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul has urged Australian businesses to invest in Thailand, touting the nation as a gateway to the 700-million-strong Asean market.</p>

data.title: Swiss citizen hands back lost Ban Chiang artefacts
data.description: <p>A Swiss national has handed over a collection of artefacts believed to be from the Ban Chiang archaeological site in Udon Thani to the Thai embassy in Bern for verification before their return to Thailand.</p>

data.title: Bottlenecks at Suvarnabhumi targeted before high season
data.description: <p>Deputy Prime Minister Suphajee Suthumpun has ordered urgent action to ease bottlenecks facing arriving passengers at Suvarnabhumi International Airport, targeting delays at immigration, baggage collection and on public transport.</p>

data.title: Pardon rules under review
data.description: <p>Critics have questioned the fairness of Thailand's justice system after the early release of former drug lord Laota Saenlee, whose life sentence was reduced to less than 10 years.</p>

data.title: Govt mulls firearms amnesty
data.description: <p>The government is considering allowing people to surrender illegally held firearms without facing criminal charges as part of tighter gun controls.</p>

data.title: Bangkok fitness coach dies after collapsing at Hyrox event
data.description: Bangkok-based fitness coach Leroy Saunders has died after collapsing and losing consciousness during the Hyrox Bangkok 2026 competition last Thursday, his family said on Tuesday.

data.title: Death toll from Bangkok pub fire rises to 41
data.description: Two more people have succumbed to injuries suffered in a fire at a Bangkok beer hall last month, bringing the death toll to 41, authorities said on Tuesday.

data.title: Israeli businesses on Phuket in crosshairs
data.description: PHUKET - Provincial authorities say they are investigating complaints that some businesses operated by Israelis on this tourist island are refusing services to Thai customers.

data.title: 'It's my job,' says officer who ticketed upset Malaysian biker
data.description: SONGKHLA - A Thai police officer targeted by a Malaysian biker who called on followers to boycott Thailand after he and his friends were pulled over and ticketed for a range of offences in Hat Yai has defended his actions, insisting he was only doing his legal duty.

data.title: Bogus ‘pink card’ racket broken up in Bangkok
data.description: Thai authorities have arrested seven people, including three civil servants, after uncovering the fraudulent registration of hundreds of foreign children at the Din Daeng Flats in Bangkok.

data.title: Photos with peace signs may reveal fingerprint data, ministry warns
data.description: A simple peace sign in a social media photo could expose sensitive biometric data to cybercriminals, Thailand’s Interior Ministry has warned, as advances in artificial intelligence (AI) and smartphone camera technology make it easier to extract fingerprint details from high-resolution images.

data.title: Andaman tsunami buoy to be replaced in November
data.description: <p>A tsunami-monitoring buoy off the Andaman coast will be replaced in November after it stopped transmitting data, with officials blaming possible damage from strong southwest monsoon waves.</p>

data.title: Spot checks reveal misuse of school lunch programme funds
data.description: SURAT THANI - Surprise inspections by anti-corruption officials at six schools have uncovered irregularities in the schools' student-lunch programmes, including mismanagement of funds and poor nutrition.

data.title: Some gun dealers have switched businesses to survive
data.description: Loaves of sourdough bread now fill the display window of Suchart and Friends Gun, a firearms shop-turned-bakery in Bangkok's old quarter where pistols and rifles once lined the glass case.

data.title: Volunteer clinic treats over  1,000 people in Ayutthaya
data.description: <p>A volunteer medical unit provided free healthcare to 1,037 people in Ayutthaya on Sunday, more than double its initial target of 500.</p>

data.title: Govt to replace Andaman tsunami buoy 'in November'
data.description: <p>A tsunami-monitoring buoy off the Andaman coast will be replaced in November after it stopped transmitting data, with officials blaming possible damage from strong southwest monsoon waves.</p>

data.title: South bridge deals to be inked Aug 31
data.description: <p>Contracts for two major bridge projects in the South are expected to be signed on Aug 31, with construction scheduled to begin this year and both bridges due to open in August 2029.</p>

data.title: 53 firms probed in nominee crackdown
data.description: <p>Fifty-three companies in Sakon Nakhon are being investigated for allegedly using Thai nominees to conceal Chinese ownership, Deputy Interior Minister Polapee Suwunchwee said yesterday.</p>

data.title: Three cuffed over ties to fake tax invoices network
data.description: <p>Three people have been arrested for allegedly selling fake tax invoices to businesses seeking to reduce their tax bills, with investigators saying the network had operated for about five years.</p>

data.title: Udon Thani to be medical tech hub
data.description: <p>The government is moving to establish Udon Thani as an "Innovation Sandbox" for Thai medical technology, initially introducing four products from the Thai Innovation Account into the national healthcare system under the universal 30-baht scheme.</p>

data.title: Lives at risk in war on pollution
data.description: <p>For years, residents of Prachin Buri have fought industrial waste pollution that they say has contaminated farmland and waterways. But for some leading the fight, protecting their communities has come at a far higher price: threats to their lives.</p>

data.title: Anutin sets limits for censure debate
data.description: <p>Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul said his ministers were ready for a no-confidence debate but would not answer for Senate election allegations he called unrelated to the government.</p>

data.title: PM to boost relations with Australia, NZ
data.description: <p>Thailand will seek to expand trade, investment, technology and creative-economy cooperation with Australia and New Zealand during Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul's visits to the two countries.</p>

data.title: Probe into civil exam fraud widens
data.description: <p>Police have charged senior officials over alleged fraud in local government recruitment examinations and are expanding the investigation to include brokers and others suspected of involvement in the scheme.</p>

data.title: Thailand to 'stay neutral' in US-China AI race
data.description: Thailand would maintain its neutral position between the United States and China and resist pressure to choose sides in the global race for artificial intelligence (AI), Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul said on Monday.

data.title: PM denies staging stop in Buri Ram
data.description: Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul has denied suggestions that a police inspection of his vehicle in Buri Ram was staged, saying officers were simply performing their duties at a routine checkpoint.

data.title: Marine agency AI art contest sparks backlash
data.description: Strong criticisms were lobbed at the Department of Marine and Coastal Resources after it announced the results of an AI art contest held to mark National Dugong Conservation Day on Monday, with the winning image showing a dugong with what appeared to be four legs.
